Teaser Trailer | Streaming January 20 on Disney+}} **[[Thrawn's forces]] }} {{Quote|Warrior-like men, witches—this place is all kinds of fun.|Anakin Skywalker, sarcastically|}} '''Dathomir''' was a remote, verdant, and dangerous [[planet]] of the [[Dathomir system]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories]]' [[Quelii sector]]. Strongly influenced by the [[dark side of the Force]], the world had varied terrains all dimly bathed in [[Color|blood-red]] light, and it was home to plenty of vegetation and predators who [[Diet|preyed]] on each other. Among them were [[rancor]]s and the [[Dathomirian]]s. Several [[Dathomiri clan]]s practiced [[magick]], including the [[Nightsisters]], and these Dathomiri [[witch]]es dominated their [[Nightbrothers|Nightbrother]] warriors and eventually attracted the attention of the [[Sith]]. The planet that would be known as Dathomir was once the seat of power of [[Kujet]], the tyrant who caused the decline of the interplanetary [[Zeffonian]] civilization. Kujet gave his followers false promises of power over [[the Force]] and massacred rebels at his [[Tomb of Kujet|palace]] on the planet, which was left steeped in darkness and abandoned after his death. At some point, the Nightsisters arrived and formed a [[Symbiosis|symbiotic]] relationship with the rancors to drive out the [[Fromprath]], the [[Homeworld|native]] [[Sentience|sentient]] [[Reptile|reptilians]]. The Nightsisters—linked to the ancient [[Witch Kingdom of the Dathmiri]] on [[Peridea]] in the [[far galaxy]]—then named their planet "Dathomir." At another point, legends claimed that a [[Jedi]] named [[Allya]] was [[Exile (punishment)|exiled]] to Dathomir, where she taught its women the ways of the Force. Leading up to the rise of the [[Galactic Empire]], Dathomir was involved in multiple tragedies amidst the machinations of [[Mother (title)|Mother]] [[Talzin]] of the Nightsisters and the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Sidious]]. Talzin was a powerful spellcaster who unified the Dathomiri clans, and Sidious took away her son, [[Maul]], to be trained as a [[Sith Lord]] away from Dathomir. After Maul fell in battle, Sidious' next apprentice, [[Sith apprentice|apprentice]], [[Count of Serenno|Count]] [[Dooku]], trained the Nightsister [[Asajj Ventress]] as his [[Sith acolyte|disciple]]. Upon being [[Battle of Sullust|abandoned]] during the [[Clone Wars]], in which Dathomir remained neutral between the [[Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatists]], Ventress found her way back to her people. However, their plots to take revenge upon the Sith ultimately led to the [[Battle of Dathomir|massacre]] of most of the Nightsisters on Dathomir by the [[Separatist Droid Army]]. A few surviving Dathomirians roamed [[the galaxy]]. This included Ventress, who embraced the [[light side of the Force]] after regretting pushing [[Quinlan Vos]], a [[Jedi Master]] and her lover, to the dark side on Dathomir. As part of his quest for revenge against the Sith, Maul briefly brought [[Ezra Bridger]], a Jedi member of the [[Spectres]] anti-Empire rebel cell, to Dathomir. Other Dathomirian survivors included [[Merrin]] and [[Shelish]]. There was also [[Morgan Elsbeth]], who served the Imperial [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]] even after the fall of Darth Sidious as [[Galactic Emperor]]. Thrawn allied with the [[Great Mothers]] on Peridea and then set up his [[Thrawn's forces|forces]] at Dathomir. They thus waged [[Campaign against Thrawn's forces|war]] against the [[New Republic]], including against forces led by the former Spectres. ==Description== {{Quote|Dathomir is a dangerous world inhabited by a number of deadly creatures, such as the chirodactyl, an apex predator.|Darth Sidious|}} [[File:Nightfall-DC.png|thumb|left|300px|Dathomir was home to several dangerous predators, such as the rancor and the chirodactyl.]] Dathomir was a remote and uninviting [[Planet|world]]{{Databank|dathomir|Dathomir}} filled with a verdant and dangerous ecosystem. The planet completed an [[orbit]] around its [[red dwarf]] [[Star|sun]] [[Domir]] every 491 [[Standard day|days]], each spanning 24 [[Standard hour|hours]]. Domir cast a [[Color|blood-red]] light across the [[Dathomir system]], which occupied the [[Quelii sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories]]' [[New Territories]], within grid square O-6 of the [[Standard Galactic Grid]]. Perpetually bathed in a red mist, Dathomir's terrain was one of contrasts, ranging from the murky [[swamp]]s the [[Nightsisters]] lived in to the harsh, barren rocks where the [[Nightbrothers]] found residence. While it was orbited by four moons, Dathomir had a low gravity and a temperate and breathable [[atmosphere]], with a diameter spanning 10,460 [[kilometer]]s. The planet's surface had rocky features, including [[mountain]]s alongside [[cave]]s and cliffs, canyons and valleys.''[[Collapse of the Republic]]'' Dathomir also had savannahs, tar-pits, and [[Water|ice]] caps. However, many lifeforms grew and survived by the rivers, waterfalls, and pools of Dathomir, with [[swamp]]s and [[forest]]s providing shelter.
[[File:DathomiriRancorPrestige-Homeworlds.png|thumb|right|250px|Rancors were native to Dathomir.]]
Besides the [[rancor]], other native creatures included [[Bane Back Spider|bane back spider]]s, large and aggressive [[Spider|arachnids]] that spat corrosive [[acid]], and [[Lesser Nydak|nydaks]], bipedal predators with powerful [[Limb|arms]] that allowed them to easily traverse the landscape. Among the most distinctive creatures native to Dathomir, however, was the [[chirodactyl]], a species of gigantic [[bat]] that used its massive wings to fly to high heights and swoop down on unwary prey. One example of this species, [[Gorgara]], was known by the native Nightbrothers as "the winged daemon of the canyon" and was particularly feared by them. Dathomir also had [[Water|aquatic]] life, such as the [[Burra fish]]. [[Fishing]] families on the [[planet]] Batuu cooked and cultivated the foreign Burra fish for consumption.[[Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge|''Star Wars'': Galaxy's Edge]] has official backstory elements that, though not directly published for the public, are officially canon details that can be obtained verbally from cast members working in the land. Another aquatic creature, [[the Sleeper]], was an ancient [[mollusk]] with two large [[Color|lavender]] [[eye]]s, a carapace-covered body, [[antenna]]e, and four [[Limb|appendages]], and lived deep in the murky blue water within the [[Nightsister lair]]. The Sleeper was very important in Nightsister [[Nightsisters#Society and culture|tradition]] as it had an ingredient vital in the [[Water of Life]]. Not many [[Dathomirian]]s left the planet, and those elsewhere in [[the galaxy]] rarely visited it.{{SW|url=news/star-wars-inside-intel-the-nightsisters|text=''Star Wars'' Inside Intel: The Nightsisters|int=Star Wars Inside Intel}} ==History== ===The tyranny of Kujet and the Witch Kingdom=== {{Quote|My friend, I have never been one to shy away from the pursuit of knowledge, but the shadow of the dark side lies heavy in this tomb. I've uncovered Kujet's legacy: a ruthless leader who destroyed the Astriums and lives of any who opposed the sage's rule. These Zeffo were once Kujet's enemies, brave rebels who stood against tyranny. F-forgive me. I've spent too many rotations on this planet. My mind is beginning to slip. I can go no further. I must return to Zeffo.|Eno Cordova|}} [[File:DathomirRuins.png|thumb|left|260px|Kujet's palace on Dathomir]] In ancient [[time]]s before the [[Galactic Empire]], the [[Zeffonian]] civilization of the [[planet]] [[Zeffo]] reached its height of power, with the [[Zeffo Sage]] [[Kujet]] building an imposing [[Tomb of Kujet|palace]] on the planet that would be later known as Dathomir. It served as Kujet's secluded seat of power as the sage became ruthless and cruel. He promised his followers power over the mystical energy field known to them as "[[The Force|the Life Wind]]" and destroyed all Life Wind–channelling [[Astrium]]s apart from the one that he held. The tyrant also staged a massacre of rebels against his rule at his palace. Kujet's greed caused the collapse of the Zeffo civilization, and he was entombed in his own palace, which was left abandoned as it remained shadowed in the [[dark side of the Force]]. Kujet's name was engraved in runes at the [[Great Mothers' Fortress]] on [[Peridea]], a planet in [[Far galaxy|another galaxy]] home to the [[Witch Kingdom of the Dathmiri]], which was the civilization from which the people who called themselves the "Nightsisters" were descended.{{Ahsoka|Part Six: Far, Far Away}}{{Databank|peridea|Peridea}} According to legend, the ancient Nightsisters [[Taming beasts|connected]] with the [[purrgil]] "space-whales" and rode them through the dimension of [[hyperspace]], travelling [[Pathway to Peridea|between]] [[Galaxy|galaxies]]. Having existed before the [[Jedi Order]] was founded{{HomeVideoCite|set=Ahsoka: The Complete First Season|featurette=Darkness Rising}} around [[25,025 BBY]], the three [[Great Mothers]] [[Klothow]], [[Aktropaw]], and [[Lakesis]] went into hibernation before Peridea's galaxy was devastated in a [[Far galaxy war|war]]. At some point in the other galaxy, the Nightsisters arrived on the homeworld of the [[Sentience|sentient]] [[Reptile|reptilians]] called the [[Fromprath]] and drove them out, naming the planet "Dathomir" in honor of their origins.''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' In order to claim the world from the Fromprath, the Nightsisters formed a [[Symbiosis|symbiotic]] relationship with the rancors.''[[Star Wars: The Dark Side]]'' [[File:NightsisterFortress-Rebels.png|thumb|right|300px|Elongated faces and figures adorned the stone structures of the Nightsisters of Dathomir.]] The ancient Nightsisters also built a [[Nightsisters' Temple|temple]] of stone on the planet [[Arcana]] in Dathomir's galaxy,{{Ahsoka|Part One: Master and Apprentice}} as well as a [[Seatos reflex point|stone henge]] on the planet [[Seatos]].{{Ahsoka|Part Two: Toil and Trouble}} On Dathomir itself, the Dathomirian matriarchs kept the male Nightbrothers as warriors and mates in their own villages while the Nightsisters lived in stone structures that commonly featured elongated female faces such as that of [[Witches Horn]], at the peak of the [[Strangled Cliffs]]. The [[Zabrak]] Nightbrothers lived in multi-storey buildings erected on rocky terrain and were of the same overall species as the [[Iridonian]] Zabraks of the planet [[Iridonia]]. However, the species' wide colonization efforts meant that the Dathomirian Zabraks called Dathomir, rather than Iridonia, home.{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/monster-trivia-gallery|text="Monster" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 3}} Dathomir's Nightsisters claimed to speak [[Paecian]], mixing that language from the world of [[Paecia]] in the nearby [[Quelii sector]]{{GalaxyMapAppendix}} — Based on corresponding data for the [[Paecia system]] with [[Galactic Basic Standard]]. They also spoke spells in [[Dathomirian language|another language]]. ===Beyond the Republic=== Dathomir was not part of the [[Galactic Republic]], which ruled much of the galaxy and was defended by the Jedi Order, who were trained to heed the [[light side of the Force]] and be the guardians of peace and justice for [[Living Force|all life]].''[[The Star Wars Book]]'' The Republic dropped off some of its [[prisoner]]s and criminals on Dathomir. According to legend, in [[600 BBY]],{{BuildFalconCite|59|Guide to the Galaxy}} the [[Jedi]] [[Allya]] was [[Exile (punishment)|exiled]] to Dathomir, where she taught the women there the ways of the Force. The Nightsisters practiced [[magick]], an aspect of the Force that manifested as [[Color|green]] mist, and they drew strength from their connection to their planet. The Nightsisters revered both the [[Winged Goddess]] of life, divination, and fertility and the [[Fanged God]] of death and the hunt. Prior to the Clone Wars, [[OteroaCorp]] created their twentieth settlement on Dathomir. [[Oteroa Zero-Twenty]] was located in a [[jungle]] near the [[Nardithi Cluster]]. An OteroaCorp [[Starship|ship]] called the ''[[The Oteroan Sky]]'' [[Crash of The Oteroan Sky|crashed]] after it was sabotaged by the [[Nardithi Nightsisters]] and it crashed into the city, destroying it. ===The legend of the gilded cage=== [[File:TheGildedCage-DL.png|thumb|right|300px|The Nightsisters of Dathomir met Darth Caldoth.]] According to legend, there was a [[Sith]] named [[Darth Caldoth]] who stole a Nightsister [[burial pod]] on the planet to learn the secrets of the Nightsister reanimation process. Because of this, the Nightsisters patiently waited and plotted till Caldoth was defeated at a Jedi Temple on [[Bathoris]]. After Caldoth's defeat by [[Jedi Master]] [[Bran Ath'Morath]], the Nightsisters called for a gathering on the planet at night time. During the gathering, six Nightsisters were chosen and bound to pillars while they were attacked by the spirits of dead Nightsisters. One Nightsister called [[Zeldin]] successfully managed to survive through the night. Then the very next night, the Nightsister coven gathered and added their voices to support Zeldin as she enacted a ritual to persuade and influence Caldoth into doing the Nightsisters bidding.{{StoryCite|story=The Gilded Cage|book=Dark Legends}} The ritual worked and Zeldin, while in a deep trance, slowly and carefully influenced Caldoth. The Nightsisters later enacted a ritual of prognostication for a glimpse into the future. Learning that Caldoth would take a male [[Twi'lek]] named [[Ry Nymbis]] as his [[Sith apprentice|apprentice]], Zeldin infiltrated Caldoth's mind in the hopes that Nymbis would betray and kill Caldoth. This failed however leading to the Nightsisters performing another ritual of prognostication on Dathomir. Because of this, the Nightsisters were aware of an old totem guarded by the guardian spirit of one of the ancient monks of a temple on the [[Unknown Regions]] moon [[Obsidia]]. Knowing that the Guardian spirit could obliterate Caldoth, Zeldin carefully extended her influence in Caldoths mind and pointed him towards an ancient tablet containing the location of the old totem. However once again, Caldoth managed to escape his demise by using the Nightsisters binding ritual to trap the Guardian spirit. Annoyed, the Nightsisters performed a final ritual and gained insight into the future of Caldoth where Caldoth was seemingly killed by his enemy, Morath. Armed with this knowledge, Zeldin once again steered Caldoth into seeking revenge on Morath for beating him on Bathoris. The plan failed however and Morath was instead beheaded by Caldoth in the city of [[Pundith]] on the world of [[Kizan]]. Frustrated, the Nightsisters attempted to perform a ritual to turn Caldoth into a prisoner of the Nightsisters. Instead Zeldin, while attempting to break the mental barriers of Caldoth's mind, became trapped in Caldoth's mind. From that day onwards, the Nightsisters did not come to Zeldin's aid and instead put Zeldin's body in a Nightsister burial pod. It was later hung in the exact same spot as the previous burial pod taken by Caldoth. After the incident, Caldoth visited Zeldin time to time to hear her screams. ===Golden Age of the Dathomiri Nightsisters=== ====The lost children==== {{Quote|Long ago, Sidious came to me on Dathomir. We exchanged secret wisdom—mingled ''dark side abilities'' with ''Nightsister Magicks''. He promised to make me his right hand, but instead he ''stole'' what was most dear to me…my own flesh and blood. My son!|Mother Talzin|[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 3|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 3]]}} [[File:YoungDarthMaulSidious.png|thumb|right|170px|Talzin's young son]] [[Talzin]] became a [[Parent|mother]] in [[54 BBY]] when she [[Reproduction|gave birth]] to the Dathomirian Zabrak who would later become the infamous [[Maul]].[[Star Wars Jedi Master Magazine 1|''Star Wars Jedi Master'' Magazine 1]] [[Asajj Ventress]] was born in [[Mother Talzin's clan|Talzin's Nightsister clan]] on Dathomir in [[50 BBY]].''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]'' dates the [[Reproduction|birth]] of the [[Asajj Ventress]] amidst [[Mother Talzin's clan|Talzin's Nightsister clan]] on [[Dathomir]] to 50 [[Standard year|years]] before the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], which corresponds to [[50 BBY]] per ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''. She was given away as an infant by her [[Asajj Ventress's mother|mother]] and Talzin to the [[Siniteen]] [[pirate]] [[Hal'Sted]], as their clan was forced to surrender an infant to Hal'Sted in exchange for their own survival and safety.''[[Star Wars: Women of the Galaxy]]'' Hal'Sted then took Ventress to the war-torn world of [[Rattatak]] in the Outer Rim's [[Trilon sector]],{{GalaxyMapAppendix}} — Based on corresponding data for the [[Rattatak system]] where the lost Nightsister grew up estranged from her people. [[File:AnUnwillingApprentice-MaF.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Maul was abducted from Dathomir and trained in the ways of the Sith.]] Talzin was talented in the eldritch magicks of the Nightsisters, and she received [[Darth Sidious]] on Dathomir. While his public persona was [[Senator]] Palpatine of [[Naboo]] in the [[Galactic Senate|Republic Senate]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' Sidious was the [[Sith apprentice]] of [[Darth Plagueis]], a [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] who sought the secrets of [[immortality]] and plotted the execution of the [[Grand Plan]] of the [[Sith]]—to overthrow the Jedi and the Republic and rule the galaxy. The way of the dark side was greed for power, and Sidious and Talzin exchanged their respective knowledge of manipulating the Force on Dathomir. Sidious promised Talzin that she would become his right hand and made several visits to Dathomir, during which he frightened Talzin's first-born son.{{StoryCite|story=An Unwilling Apprentice|book=Myths & Fables}} {{C|[[Galaxy's Edge]] edition}} Around [[40 BBY]], Sidious took him to be trained as his own apprentice against Talzin's will. Sidious dubbed her son "[[Darth]] Maul" and later murdered his own [[Sith Master]].{{Databank|emperor-palpatine-darth-sidious|Emperor Palpatine/Darth Sidious}} Darth Sidious orchestrated the [[Battle of Naboo]] to elevate his public persona, Senator Palpatine, to the position of [[Supreme Chancellor]] of the Galactic Republic in [[32 BBY]]. During the battle, Maul killed [[Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn]], who had just brought [[Anakin Skywalker]], the [[Chosen One]] of Jedi prophecy, from the planet [[Tatooine]] to the Jedi Order. Maul was then defeated by Jinn's [[Padawan]] learner, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], and deemed dead by the Order, who were alerted to the return of the Sith after [[Defeat of the Sith|their defeat]] [[1032 BBY|one thousand years ago]]. However, Talzin knew that Maul lived, and her hatred for Sidious' use and then abandonment of her son grew. She remained on Dathomir as she was unaware of Maul's whereabouts, while Maul himself lost much of his sanity while desiring to return to Talzin at Dathomir's [[Mount Gethzerion]].[[Star Wars Adventures: Return to Vader's Castle 1|''Star Wars Adventures: Return to Vader's Castle'' 1]] ====Contact with the Jedi==== As the Sith's galactic plans matured, Talzin made her own ascent to power on Dathomir. She unified her world's Nightsister clans after the fall of [[Mother (title)|Mother]] [[Zalem]].{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Chrome Perspectives|subset=Jedi Temple Archives|cardname=Mother Talzin|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/114595/cid/8022653/2015-Topps-Star-Wars-Chrome-Perspectives:-Jedi-Vs.-Sith-49-J-Mother-Talzin}} Zalem died following a confrontation with the Jedi [[Quinlan Vos]] at some point before the [[Clone Wars]].{{BuildFalconCite|59|Guide to the Galaxy}} Also at some point before the wars, Jedi Master [[Eno Cordova]] explored Dathomir for relics of the Zeffo civilization and discovered the Tomb of Kujet. [[File:TalzinDooku-Monster.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Mother Talzin once received help from Dooku, though she kept her homeworld clear of the Republic and the Sith.]] At another point before the Clone Wars, Talzin received help from [[Dooku]], the [[Count of Serenno]] and former Jedi who trained Qui-Gon Jinn. Darth Sidious took Dooku as his new apprentice upon Maul's defeat,{{TOTJ|The Sith Lord}} and the count's search for a [[Dark Acolyte]] of his own eventually led him to Asajj Ventress on Rattatak. He cultivated Ventress' hatred for the Jedi; Ventress wrongly believed that the Jedi abandoned her master, [[Ky Narec]], the first to help Ventress hone her strong connection to the Force through Jedi ways rather than through the magick of Dathomir.''[[Dooku: Jedi Lost]]'' The Jedi of the Republic were aware of the Nightsisters and their use of dark magicks, but they gave the witches a wide berth as the sisters remained focused on matters on Dathomir.{{Databank|nightsisters|Nightsisters}} With the Nightsisters regarding all outsiders with suspicion, Mother Talzin kept Dathomir clear of the Republic and, with Dooku spearheading the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatist movement]] across the galaxy, clear of the Separatist Alliance too. The Clone Wars broke out between the two factions in [[22 BBY]] under Darth Sidious' scheming. ====The mists of vengeance==== [[File:VentressFoundOnDathomir-Nightsisters.jpg|thumb|left|350px|Ventress found her fellow Nightsisters after being abandoned by the Sith.]] As Ventress led her [[Asajj Ventress's fleet|Separatist fleet]] at the [[Battle of Sullust]] against [[Republic Navy|Republic forces]] led by Master Obi-Wan Kenobi and [[Jedi Knight]] Anakin Skywalker in [[20 BBY]], Sidious ordered Dooku to eliminate his [[Sith acolyte|acolyte]]. Ventress survived her master's betrayal and found her way back her sisters on Dathomir, where she was cared for by Mother Talzin. Talzin and Ventress then plotted in their coven's [[Nightsister lair|stone fortress]] to [[assassin]]ate Dooku. Talzin sent her clan's greatest warriors, the [[Hunter (Nightsister)|Hunters]] [[Naa'leth]] and [[Karis]], to accompany Ventress to [[Castle Serenno|Dooku's castle]] on his homeworld [[Serenno]]. Their [[Mission to Serenno (Nightsisters)|assassination]] attempt failed, though the three Nightsisters concealed their identities and survived to return to Dathomir. Talzin then plotted a more elaborate plan that involved inviting Dooku to Dathomir. Contacting the count via [[hologram]], Mother Talzin offered to supply him with a Nightbrother for training as his new disciple. [[File:OpressWarriorTest-Monster.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Savage Opress in the Selection]] Dooku landed on Dathomir with his [[Count Dooku's solar sailer|solar sailer]] and was received at the Nightsister fortress. Although he proposed that Mother Talzin's coven could join his Separatist Alliance, the witch rejected the offer by asserting that the Nightsisters were loyal only to themselves. She then lied to Dooku that she was helping him find a suitable Nightbrother in return for the count having helped her a long time ago. Meanwhile, Ventress had travelled to the far side of the planet on a [[Nightsister speeder]] made by [[Ubrikkian Transports]]''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia of Starfighters and Other Vehicles]]'' to the [[Nightbrother village|village]] of the Nightbrothers. She chose several men to take part in the [[Selection]], a series of trials in their [[Nightbrother arena|arena]]. After killing several of the Nightbrothers in ritual combat, Ventress chose Talzin’s younger son and Maul’s brother [[Savage Opress]]. Ventress then took Opress to the Nightsisters' lair, where they used their magick to augment Opress' strength and power. After Opress demonstrated his loyalty by killing his [[Feral|younger brother]], Talzin gave him to Dooku. After Dooku sent his new acolyte on a [[Devaron massacre|rampage]] against the Jedi and Republic on the planet [[Devaron]], the Jedi Order's [[Jedi High Council|High Council]] was alarmed by what they saw as the appearance of a Dathomirian Zabrak similar to the [[Sith Lord]] that Master Kenobi had struck down on Naboo over a [[Standard decade|decade]] ago. Masters [[Yoda]] and [[Mace Windu]] therefore sent Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker to investigate further on Dathomir. They found the Nightbrother village and asked about Opress' whereabouts, with Brother [[Viscus]] answering that one of Talzin's Nightsisters took him as a mate to their fortress. Kenobi and Skywalker then met with the Clan Mother, who obliged their questions and used her [[Nightsister crystal ball|crystal ball]] to locate Opress on the planet [[Toydaria]]. The Jedi then left Dathomir and failed to stop Opress in a [[Showdown at Toydaria|battle]] over Toydaria that also involved Ventress and Dooku. Opress became distressed by the latter two's competing and demanding instructions, and he fled back to Talzin on Dathomir. The Clan Mother then gave Opress a greater and more personal purpose—to return his long-lost brother Maul to Dathomir. Ventress later returned to Dathomir too, with Talzin and the Nightsisters welcoming her back into their midst. She underwent her initiation as a Nightsister at their fortress, entering the Water of Life to face the ancient Sleeper. Ventress entered as a Sith and felt that she was reborn after meeting the Sleeper, as she chose to leave her Sith past behind and accept the love of her sisters. During the initiation festivities, a [[Separatist Droid Army|Droid Army]] sent by Count Dooku arrived on their world. ===Massacre=== {{Main|Battle of Dathomir}} [[File:BattleOfDathomir-Massacre.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Nightsisters summon their Army of the Dead to defend against the Separatists.]] The army was led by the Separatists' [[Supreme Martial Commander of the Separatist Droid Armies|Supreme Commander]], [[General]] [[Grievous]], and included the [[Defoliator Deployment Tank]]. Mother Talzin and her coven's even more powerful elder, "Old [[Daka]]," raised their [[Army of the Dead]] to help defend against the [[droid]] forces before their fortress, but the [[Battle of Dathomir]] became a massacre. Although Talzin also tormented Dooku from afar via [[voodoo]] and Ventress attempted to [[Lightsaber duel|duel]] Grievous, the [[battle droid]]s continued overwhelming the Nightsisters, and Grievous forced his way into their [[Hidden Cave]] to strike a lethal blow upon Daka. Talzin retreated to the [[spirit world]] before Grievous could strike likewise, while most of the Nightsisters fell in battle. Among the fallen were Naa'leth, Karis, [[Talia (Nightsister)|Talia]], [[Luce]], and [[Selena]]. The latter's daughter, [[Morgan Elsbeth]], survived and believed she was the last Nightsister when the Dathomirian [[human]]s of the peaceful [[Mountain Clan]] took her in. Against the advice of the [[Mountain Clan Matron]], Morgan Elsbeth convinced some clan members to help her salvage some Nightsister weapons. This led them into a deadly skirmish with [[Confederacy military|Separatist forces]] that killed a [[Nali|daughter of the Matron]], who pitied Elsbeth's dark future and abandoned her in Dathomir's forests.{{TOTE|The Path of Fear}} Another survivor was the Nightsister [[Yenna]], who was made of material such as [[clay]] by the magick of the clanless witch [[Falta]]. Talzin had Yenna placed in a [[Escape pod|lifepod]] during the battle, and the pod launched from Dathomir toward the Mid Rim. When Falta searched the ruins of the Nightsister lair soon after the massacre, the dying Daka directed her to find Yenna off-world. There was also the child [[Merrin]], who buried her fellow Nightsisters, including her lover [[Ilyana]]. Merrin believed herself to be the last Nightsister, and she eventually made contact with the Nightbrothers, who were led by Brother Viscus. As for Ventress, she also survived the massacre she had tried to stop and spoke with Mother Talzin, who appeared from the spirit world as a green mist. Talzin told Ventress that she must walk her own path and then, despite Ventress' pleas for her to stay by her side, quickly dissipated. Ventress subsequently made her way from Dathomir to Tatooine and became a [[bounty hunter]].{{TCW|Bounty (episode)}} ===Dathomir's children=== ====Return of Maul==== Talzin focused on guiding Opress in their search for Maul, who was found with a broken body and mind on the junk moon of [[Lotho Minor]]. When Opress returned to Dathomir's ruined Nightsister lair with Maul in tow, Talzin received them and restored Maul's sanity. The mother further used her magick to make new [[Limb|legs]] for her first-born son out of droid parts before retreating to the spirit world again. After Opress explained to his brother the events that had transpired, Maul took him as his apprentice and vowed to take revenge against Obi-Wan Kenobi and Darth Sidious. This led them on violent campaigns off-world.{{TCW|Revenge (episode)}} Maul and Opress eventually found [[Death Watch|Mandalorian terrorists]] opposed to [[Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze]]'s pacifist government on [[Mandalore]] in the Outer Rim. In [[19 BBY]], Maul gathered a [[Shadow Collective]] of the galaxy's criminal underworld to [[Takeover of Mandalore|conquer]] Mandalore and [[Battle of Mandalore|lure out]] Kryze's lover, who was Obi-Wan Kenobi. However, Darth Sidious was wary of his former apprentice's growing power and personally captured Maul after slaying Opress.[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 1|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 1]] ====Spectre of Talzin==== Mother Talzin turned her focus away from her sons of Dathomir and onto the [[Frangawl Cult]] instead. The cult operated within the [[Colonies]] region, on the worlds [[Bardotta]] and [[Zardossa Stix]], and they kidnapped the [[Dagoyan Order|Dagoyan Masters]] to drain their life force into{{TCW|The Disappeared, Part II}} the Nightsisters' [[Bardottan Sphere]] at the behest of Talzin.''[[Nexus of Power]]'' Talzin left Dathomir to appear on Zardossa Stix for the [[Frangawl sacrificial ceremony|ceremony]] that she hoped would restore her powers, but before her cult could sacrifice the [[Bardottan]] [[queen]], [[Julia]], Jedi Master Mace Windu and Queen Julia's lover and Naboo [[Junior Representative|representative]] [[Jar Jar Binks]] jointly [[Mission to Zardossa Stix|foiled]] the plan. The Nightsister drew the [[Blade of Talzin]] in defense and disappeared back into the spirit world on Dathomir to stay alive. ====Ventress and Vos==== Asajj Ventress' life as a bounty hunter did not stop bringing her back into the crosshairs of the Jedi Order. When its High Council, fatigued by war and in desperation, tasked Jedi Master Quinlan Vos with [[Mission to assassinate Count Dooku|assassinating]] Count Dooku, the Council first asked Vos to enlist the help of Ventress. During their ventures together, the pair fell in love with each other, and Ventress committed herself to Vos' mission. She believed that the only way to defeat Dooku was to grasp the dark side of the Force, but only in the way of the Nightsisters, as she believed that they could use dark powers without losing themselves, as opposed to the Sith way. They therefore traveled to Dathomir. After landing at a distance from Ventress' old home village with her starship, the [[Banshee (starship)|''Banshee'']], the pair discussed Ventress' past, including her times on her planet. [[File:Dathomir_Disciple.jpg|thumb|left|350px|Asajj Ventress puts Quinlan Vos through trials on Dathomir.]] They also spoke about Vos' past, including how he lost his master, [[Tholme]]. Both to hide her own responsibility and to manipulate Vos' emotions, Ventress lied that Dooku killed Tholme. Wrapped in mutual desire and anguish, Ventress and Vos spent many subsequent days on Dathomir. They buried Ventress' fallen sisters near their campsite. They slept and climbed and hunted and ran. Several days after arrival, Ventress took Vos on a run toward the fortress of her coven. She said that Vos was not yet ready to enter it, and she herself kept quiet on their run back to their camp. Ventress then made Vos provoke and fight surrounding innocent creatures, turning pain and anger into hatred. One day, she tested Vos in a lightsaber duel, which brought them to the Nightsister fortress, and announced that he must face the Sleeper, the ancient creature of the Water of Life that Nightsisters faced at the end of their initiation trials. They spoke about the Sleeper that night, looking forward to Vos' trials in Dathomir's oceans. As his training progressed, the pair spoke on another evening about the hypothetical future after killing Dooku, and they affirmed that they wanted to be with each other. Vos destroyed his [[holocomm]] that linked him to the Jedi to signify that he would leave the Order if it [[Jedi Code|forbade]] him from staying with Ventress, and the pair joyously embraced each other, with Vos taking Ventress in his arms and striding toward the ''Banshee''. Just then, Ventress' [[Sumdin|informant]] contacted her to confirm Dooku's exact location at a future time. Although she was worried that Vos was not yet ready, he assured her that he could take on the Sleeper, and so they walked to the Water of Life. Vos awakened the Sleeper and Ventress urged her lover to kill it. Vos made the Sleeper obey his commands and resisted killing it, protesting that it was an innocent creature and possibly the last of its kind. Ventress accepted that it may die with a great secret of her clan but claimed that it was necessary for Vos to slay it, reasoning that if he could not do so, then he could not kill Dooku in cold blood and thus allow his Jedi compassion to "ruin everything." Vos finally gave in to his emotions and killed the Sleeper. With Vos' Nightsister training complete, the pair left Dathomir on the ''Banshee'' and headed to the Separatist capital world of [[Raxus Secundus]], where they faced Dooku and Grievous. Vos was captured by Dooku, who exploited the Jedi's emotional vulnerabilities, particularly over how Tholme had actually been killed by Ventress, to corrupt Vos into a Separatist enforcer known as [[Admiral]] Enigma. ====The final showdown==== Maul was freed from Sith captivity by his loyal [[Mandalorian super commando]]s, led by [[Gar Saxon]] and [[Rook Kast]]. They rebuilt the Shadow Collective and recruited Nightbrothers from Dathomir, with a shuttle's worth of Nightbrothers joining just in time for the [[Battle on Ord Mantell|Battle of Ord Mantell]], where they captured both Count Dooku and General Grievous.[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 2|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 2]] Darth Sidious, as Chancellor Palpatine, then dispatched the Jedi and the Republic to [[Assault on Vizsla Keep 09|battle]] Maul and his forces, who then retreated. With Dooku still in tow, Maul and his forces traveled to Dathomir, landing at the Nightbrothers' village. There, Mother Talzin tried to drain Dooku's life force to become stronger than ever before. However, Darth Sidious promptly arrived along with Grievous and his droid army. At this [[Second Battle of Dathomir]], Maul's forces on Dathomir came under attack without being reinforced by the forces of [[Black Sun]] and the [[Pyke Syndicate]]. Although Mother Talzin restored her physical form, she perished in battle against Sidious and Grievous in the process of saving her son. Maul was distraught as his surviving commandos fled with him off Dathomir, with the Nightbrothers' village ruined. Dathomir was left to the conquerors. ====At war's end==== {{Quote|There are two paths before you. You may join me and your sisters in this realm, or you may return to the land of the living.|Mother Talzin, to Asajj Ventress|{{TOTU|A Way Forward}}}} Ventress and Obi-Wan Kenobi eventually helped recover Quinlan Vos, who nevertheless wanted to further his mission and pose as an aspiring Sith Lord. Amidst [[Second battle of Christophsis|battle]] on the planet [[Christophsis]], Vos apprenticed himself to Dooku in order to unveil the true identity of his master, Darth Sidious. The Jedi believed that Vos remained corrupted by the dark side while Ventress stood by her lover. The Dathomirian surrendered herself to the light and encouraged Vos that it was never too late to change as Dooku dealt her a fatal blow of [[Force lightning]]. Moved by his lover's compassion and selfless sacrifice, Vos refused Dooku's goading to give into the dark side again and comforted Ventress instead of pursuing Dooku, who was rescued by Sidious. [[File:AWayForward-QuinlanSaysGoodbye.png|thumb|right|350px|Quinlan Vos and Ventress bid farewell on Dathomir.]] Upon reflections led by Obi-Wan Kenobi, the events made the Jedi High Council realize that they had lost their way, and it was a daughter of Dathomir who gave her life and restored another back to the Jedi. Kenobi and Vos therefore [[Funeral|restored]] Ventress' body to Dathomir, laying in the waters of her sisters' fortress, which accepted her before the Jedi turned to leave the world. In the realm of the dead, Mother Talzin told Ventress that she may choose whether to stay in the realm, where she would be welcomed alongside her sisters, or to return to the land of the living at the cost of her "heart's desire." Letting go of the love of her life, Ventress decided to live again, and she stepped out of her coven's lair. As for Maul and his loyalists who retreated from Dathomir, they regrouped on Mandalore, intending a desperate final attempt to foil Darth Sidious' Grand Plan by luring out Anakin Skywalker. They instead faced forces led by Skywalker's former Jedi apprentice, [[Ahsoka Tano]], at the [[Siege of Mandalore]] as Skywalker grew closer to Sidious and became Darth Vader, replacing Dooku as the final Sith apprentice. Both Maul and Tano survived the [[Great Jedi Purge|Great Purge]] at the end of the Clone Wars{{TCW|The Phantom Apprentice}} when Sidious [[Proclamation of the New Order|enthroned himself]] as [[Galactic Emperor]]. Gar Saxon, who survived both Dathomir and Mandalore, was eventually appointed the Imperial [[Viceroy]] of Mandalore.{{Rebels|Heroes of Mandalore}} ===Imperial Era=== ====Wayward visitors==== [[File:TaronMalicos-SWGoH.png|left|thumb|250px|Due to Dathomir's dark influence, Jedi Master Taron Malicos gave in to the dark side and became the leader of the Nightbrothers.]] Prior to the end of the Clone Wars, an elite Separatist unit shot down [[Jedi General]] [[Weren Dal]] over Dathomir.''[[Savage Spirits]]'' [[Fel Trech]] crash landed on the planet, becoming mentally ill with survivor's guilt. He lived in a [[cave]] located in a [[mountain]] range and had a [[distress beacon]] that generated a detectable signal. During the [[Great Jedi Purge]], the [[Jedi Master]] [[Taron Malicos]] crash landed on the desolate planet. Though he survived the crash, the strong presence of the dark side of the Force drove him insane and he eventually usurped control of the surviving Nightbrothers by killing Brother Viscus. At some point, a [[Jerserra's master|woman]] who served Darth Sidious as one of his [[Jedi hunter|Jedi-hunting]] [[Inquisitorius|Inquisitors]] arrived on Dathomir, where she discovered [[Jerserra]] of the [[Nardithi Nightsisters|Nardithi]] sect of the Nightsisters. Jerserra had witnessed the massacre of the Nightsisters and took a shard from the [[Nardithi Cluster|cluster]] of [[Force artifact]]s that her sect had steeped in the dark side with her off-world. While the Inquisitor trained Jerserra in secret to overpower the other Inquisitors, the Nightsister eventually killed her master and lived as a [[mercenary]]. [[Doctor]] [[Chelli Lona Aphra|Chelli Aphra]] and [[Just Lucky]] traveled to the planet. Lucky was left behind on Dathomir by Aphra during the visit.[[Doctor Aphra (2020) 1|''Doctor Aphra'' (2020) 1]] Around [[0 ABY]],{{ReturnVadersCastleDate}} [[Lieutenant]] [[Thom Hudd]] took [[Dathomiri spider-silk]], which were used as shrouds, from a burial site on Dathomir, not knowing it was cursed.[[Star Wars Adventures Free Comic Book Day 2019|''Star Wars Adventures'' Free Comic Book Day 2019]] ====Merrin and the fallen Jedi Order==== [[File:Cal_shows_Merrin_the_Astrium.jpg|thumb|right|250px|In 14 BBY, Merrin, a Nightsister who survived Grievous' attack, left Dathomir along with Jedi survivor Cal Kestis and his ship's crew to explore the galaxy.]] In [[14 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]'' to [[14 BBY]]. instructed by a [[hologram]] left by Cordova through his droid [[BD-1]], Jedi [[Padawan]] [[Cal Kestis]] arrived on Dathomir with his [[Stinger Mantis crew|companions]], former Knight [[Cere Junda]], Cordova's former Padawan, and Captain [[Greez Dritus]], their pilot. Kestis was confronted by Nightsister Merrin, one of the last of her kind. Merrin blamed the Jedi for the massacre that decimated her people, and did everything in her power to impede Kestis. On his way to the tomb, Kestis encountered a mysterious wanderer who warned him about the dangers the tomb posed. Ignoring him, Kestis proceeded onward, and after being forced to fight the undead Nightsisters brought back to life by Merrin, he eventually made it into the tomb. Within, he experienced a flashback where he remembered his Master [[Jaro Tapal]] sacrificing himself to protect him from the [[clone trooper]]s during the Purge, Kestis was attacked by a manifestation of Jaro's spirit, resulting in his [[Jaro Tapal's lightsaber|lightsaber]] being destroyed. After constructing a new [[Cal Kestis' second lightsaber|lightsaber]], Kestis returned to Dathomir to complete his trials. He faced Tapal's spirit again, defeating him by overcoming his feelings of guilt over his death. Malicos again attempted to sway Kestis to the dark side, and he attacked when he refused him. Merrin helped Kestis defeat Malicos by using her magick to bury him alive, and afterward she decided to join the ''[[Stinger Mantis]]'' crew. ====Crimson Dawn and the Rebellion==== [[File:QiraMaul-CrimsonReign1.jpg|left|thumb|250px|On Dathomir, Maul taught Qi'ra many secrets of the Sith.]] Maul led the criminal syndicate [[Crimson Dawn]]''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'' from his room in the Nightsister fortress on Dathomir.[[Crimson Reign 1|''Crimson Reign'' 1]] In [[10 BBY]], after the death of his minion [[Dryden Vos]], Maul summoned [[Qi'ra]], another of his underlings, to his homeworld, warning her they would be working more closely. When Qi'ra arrived on Dathomir, Maul brought her to the fortress, explaining to her everything about the Sith and he planned to destroy them for revenge since took everything from him by killing his mother and his brother. At some point, Maul's [[R3-series astromech droid]] [[R3-B0017]] was programmed to scavenge Dathomir.{{DisneyToyCite|set=Star Wars: Droid Factory (toy line)|pack=R3-BOO17|altlink=https://jedibusiness.com/figureDetails.aspx?id=12151}} Maul eventually left Lady Qi'ra in charge of Crimson Dawn as he departed Dathomir in search of artifacts that could destroy Darth Sidious.[[Hidden Empire 1|''Hidden Empire'' 1]]{{Rebels|Twilight of the Apprentice}} He became stranded on the ancient Sith world of [[Malachor]] until it was visited by the Jedi [[Ezra Bridger]] and [[Kanan Jarrus]] of the [[Spectres|Lothal rebels]] and their new friend, Ahsoka Tano, in [[3 BBY]]. After they [[Mission to Malachor|escaped]] the grasp of Darth Vader, Maul found the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|rebels]] again in [[2 BBY]], wishing to [[Holocron fusion|merge]] the knowledge of [[Sith holocron (Malachor)|Sith]] and [[Kanan Jarrus' holocron|Jedi holocrons]] for the secret of destroying the Sith. To discover this knowledge, Maul took Bridger to Dathomir for a ritual at the Nightsister fortress. [[File:SabineKananPossessed-VisionsandVoices.png|thumb|right|300px|In search of flesh and blood to rebuild their clan, ghosts of the Nightsisters possessed Jedi Knight Kanan Jarrus and Mandalorian Sabine Wren.]] Landing at the fortress with his [[Nightbrother (Gauntlet fighter)|starship]], Maul took Bridger to his chamber and picked up a pair of gauntlets, which they used to drink potions at the Nightsister lair. They realized that the key to the Sith's destruction was being held by Obi-Wan Kenobi, living in exile on Tatooine. At the end of the ritual, Nightsister spirits began their attack on mortal souls. Just then, Kanan Jarrus and [[Sabine Wren]] of Bridger's rebel family arrived and were [[Possession|possessed]] by the spirits. Bridger helped them break free while a frustrated Maul dismissed Bridger as a failed apprentice. Maul left Dathomir for the last time, heading to Tatooine, where he was finally felled in a [[Mission to Tatooine (Imperial Era)|duel]] with Obi-Wan Kenobi.{{Rebels|Twin Suns (episode)}} By that time, Dathomir was a dead planet in terms of civilization: no sentient beings called the world home, as the few survivors lived off-world. However, the Empire was rumored to have established a [[Imperial Garrison (Dathomir)|garrison]] on Dathomir. Light cruisers and exploratory craft were known to have made secret visits as the Empire had taken a quiet interest in Dathomir, despite a lack of information on Imperial records. There were no known logistics or personnel records to support the rumors. In [[1 BBY]], the rebels of [[Lothal]] led the [[Liberation of Lothal|liberation of their homeworld]] from Imperial occupation under [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]]. Ezra Bridger foiled Darth Sidious' attempt to access the [[World Between Worlds]] and rescued Ahsoka Tano from doom on Malachor. Rejecting the temptation of holding onto pasts that could no longer exist, Bridger then called upon his bond with the purrgil to spirit Thrawn and his [[flagship]], the ''[[Chimaera]]'', to parts unknown.{{Rebels|Family Reunion – and Farewell}} They would find themselves at Peridea, the origin world of the witches of Dathomir, and Thrawn awakened the Great Mothers from their slumber. According to legend, during the pivotal [[Battle of Yavin]], the [[Force spirit]] of Obi-Wan Kenobi encouraged [[Luke Skywalker]], the son of Anakin Skywalker, to trust in the guidance of the Force by saying that many worlds would be freed from the Empire's grasp. Dathomir was among the planets mentioned.''[[The Odyssey of Star Wars: An Epic Poem]]'' ====Memories of Dathomir==== Coveting power to avenge her people and destroy her enemies, the Nightsister Morgan Elsbeth turned her fear into anger, through which she sought strength. She transformed [[Calodan]] from a village in a forest on the Outer Rim planet [[Corvus]] into the heart of an [[Elsbeth's regime|industrial power]], power that she offered to the Galactic Empire. Admiral Thrawn took notice of the self-made [[magistrate]] and questioned her motive. When she explained that she sought the power of revenge to ensure her future because her people's culture and beliefs were "fading into memory," Thrawn took this daughter of Dathomir under his wing.{{TOTE|The Path of Anger}} Another Nightsister named [[Shelish]] had left Dathomir before the massacre led by the Separatists. She eventually returned to her homeworld several times in search of clues about the fate of her sisters. After discovering what had happened on Dathomir, Shelish decided to never return to her world''[[Star Wars: Uprising]]'' while continuing to honor her sisters every day.{{StoryCite|story=The Witch & the Wookiee|book=Myths & Fables}} Shelish had a daughter known as "[[Deathstick]]" who grew up in the [[Anoat sector]] and became an assassin, leading the [[Kouhun (order)|Kouhun]] order of killers.{{UprisingWeb|url=game-guide/lore|text=Game Guide: Lore}} During the [[War of the Bounty Hunters]] in [[3 ABY]], Deathstick joined Crimson Dawn under Lady Qi'ra after she told Deathstick that Emperor Palpatine was responsible for Dathomir's fall and that Crimson Dawn would topple his Empire.[[Crimson Reign 2|''Crimson Reign'' 2]] In [[4 ABY]], Darth Sidious was [[Battle of Endor|killed]] with the return of the Jedi Anakin Skywalker given the efforts of Luke Skywalker, and the Empire [[Galactic Civil War|collapsed]] under the advance of the Rebellion, which founded the [[New Republic]]. When Imperial forces of the Anoat [[sector]] refused to surrender and imposed their [[Iron Blockade]], the Dathomirians Shelish and Deathstick helped organize the [[Uprising]] to break the blockade. ===New Republic Era=== ====The ring ship of Lady Morgan==== {{Quote|My world has been burning since I was a child. Why should this one be any different?|Lady Morgan, to the people of Corvus|{{TOTE|The Path of Hate}}}} When news of the New Republic's founding spread to Caledon on Corvus, Lady Morgan refused to let go of her hate over the destruction of Dathomir and hence held onto her iron grip of her magistracy. She received the calls of the Great Mothers of Peridea, and she directed her [[Facility 301G|facility]] at the [[Santhe Shipyards|shipyards]] of the [[Core Worlds|Core World]] [[Corellia]] to construct a massive [[hyperspace transport ring]] dubbed the ''[[Eye of Sion]]'' that would retrieve Thrawn from his exile. It was not until [[9 ABY]] that the Nightsister's despotic rule was ended by Ahsoka Tano and the Mandalorian [[Din Djarin]],{{TheMandalorian|13}} though she hired the fallen Jedi and mercenary lord [[Baylan Skoll]] to [[Attack on the Vesper|free her]] from New Republic captivity. Using the [[Arcana Star Map]] from the Nightsisters' Temple on Arcana, [[Morgan Elsbeth's forces|Lady Morgan and her crew]] charted the ancient Pathway to Peridea at the [[henge]] on Seatos, where they [[Incident on Seatos|nearly killed]] their pursuer, Ahsoka Tano, who was saved when she again found herself in the World Between Worlds.{{Ahsoka|Part Four: Fallen Jedi}} The ''Eye of Sion'' successfully took the Pathway to Peridea and enabled Grand Admiral Thrawn to return to his galaxy. [[Thrawn's forces]] had loaded the Great Mothers' catacombs onto his flagship ''Chimaera'', and although Tano led a [[Battle of Peridea|battle]] against them and killed Lady Morgan, the ''Chimaera'' docked with the ''Eye of Sion'' and entered hyperspace, eventually exiting over the planet Dathomir.{{Ahsoka|Part Eight: The Jedi, the Witch, and the Warlord}} ====Heir to the Empire==== [[File:Eye-of-Sion-Dathomir.png|thumb|right|300px|Thrawn's forces gathered over Dathomir following their exile from their galaxy.]] [[Captain of the Guard|Captain]] [[Enoch]] led Thrawn's [[Thrawn's Night Trooper legion|Night Troopers]], who were sustained by Nightsister magick, on the surface of Dathomir as the Grand Admiral waged [[Campaign against Thrawn's forces|war]] against the New Republic. Thrawn's fleet, part of the broader [[Imperial Remnant]], stayed over Dathomir, where they battled the [[New Republic Defense Force|forces]] of the New Republic.{{SWYouTube|Fdar7gTQnog|Star Wars: Ahsoka Season 2 | Teaser Trailer | Streaming January 20 on Disney+}} Three [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft|U-Wings]] were deployed to Dathomir, entering the atmosphere, with Ezra Bridger leading several [[New Republic soldier|New Republic soldiers]], where Bridger soon faced Enoch.{{SWYouTube|Fdar7gTQnog|Star Wars: Ahsoka Season 2 | Teaser Trailer | Streaming January 20 on Disney+}} ====Research trips==== {{Quote|Greetings from Dathomir, home of the rancor. Speaking of which, our friend over there could use a good old teeth-cleaning, wouldn't you say.|Aree|{{GoC|Rancor}}}} Between [[34 ABY]] and [[35 ABY]],{{UltimateCookbookDate}} the adventurous [[chef]] [[Strono Tuggs|Strono "Cookie" Tuggs]] traveled to Dathomir during a culinary tour of [[the galaxy]] that he took and unearthed the ingredients necessary to cook [[Dathomirian Noodles]]. During or after that year,{{GOCDate}} the [[safari droid]] [[SF-R3]] and his companion [[cam droid]] [[CAM]] were sent by [[Galactic Society of Creature Enthusiasts]] on a mission to Dathomir in order to research how to clean a [[rancor]]'s [[Tooth|teeth]]. He used a [[bone]] to tickle the [[nose]] of the rancor, causing it to open its mouth. Aree stuck the bone in the rancor's mouth, however, it was quickly snapped in half by the rancor. Aree detached his arm and stuck it in its mouth, this time in success, and began to work on cleaning the teeth. The process was tedious, and by the end Aree had only cleaned one tooth. Disturbed by [[Unidentified blue Dathomir bird|bird]], Aree shooed it away, causing the rancor to sneeze the safari droid back again. The [[bird]]s then rushed to clean the rancor's teeth naturally in a quick and easy process. Aree came to the conclusion that the best way to clean the rancor's teeth is to let nature take its course.{{GoC|Rancor}} ==Locations== ===Nightsister lair=== {{Main|Nightsister lair}} [[File:NightsisterFortress-Nightsisters.png|thumb|right|300px|Talzin's Nightsister village]] The Nightsister lair was the [[stone]] fortress of the Nightsisters. Built into the side of a [[mountain]], the Nightsisters lived in the many stone structures inside. The opaque pools in the lair contain water vital to the Nightsisters [[magick]]s, as well as many life-forms: from tiny single-celled organisms to moderately sized fish and crustaceans, and creature known as The Sleeper. The [[Hidden Cave]] inside the structure was the home of [[Daka]]. ===Nightbrother villages=== {{Main|Nightbrother village|Unidentified Nightbrother village}} [[File:Unidentified_Nightbrother_village_from_JFO.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The Nightbrothers second village]] The [[Nightbrother village]] was the home of the Nightbrothers until its destruction in [[19 BBY]]''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' during the [[Second Battle of Dathomir]]. The village was out in the open in a natural defensive position on top of a mountain. After the destruction of their first village, the Nightbrothers built [[Unidentified Nightbrother village|another village]], where they were reigned over by the fallen Jedi [[Taron Malicos]]. ===Kujet's Tomb=== {{Main|Tomb of Kujet}} The tomb of the [[Force-sensitive]] [[Zeffo Sage]] [[Kujet]], the palace was located at the mouth of the [[Treacherous Approach]]. Designed for sacrifice and death, Kujet would cast his enemies into the pits below his Throne Room. ==Behind the scenes== ===Original conception=== {{Quote|I created the planet Dathomir so that fans could have a good source for Force users for future books, games, and movies, and that worked out well, and I got a lot of people who felt grateful that I'd actually put women in a position of power in the ''Star Wars'' universe—something that I felt was lacking in the previous movies.|David Farland, who made Dathomir for ''The Courtship of Princess Leia''|{{WebCite|url=https://www.andrewliptak.com/david-farland-wolverton-courtship-of-princess-leia|text=Remembering Star Wars author David Farland|author=Andrew Liptak|date=2022-01-21|work=[https://www.andrewliptak.com AndrewLiptak.com]|archivedate=20260216203505}} {{C|2015 interview}}}} Dathomir's first appearance in the current [[canon]] continuity was in the [[2011]] ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|season three]] episode "[[Nightsisters (episode)|Nightsisters]]," which formed a Dathomir trilogy along with the subsequent episodes "[[Monster]]" and "[[Witches of the Mist]]."{{SW|url=video/nightsisters-episode-featurette|text="Nightsisters" Episode Featurette}} [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] originated from the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity as part of [[Lucasfilm]]'s official "Expanded Universe," as a creation of [[Dave Wolverton|David Farland's]]. Writing as Dave Wolverton for [[Bantam Spectra]], Farland made Dathomir the main setting of his April [[1994]] novel ''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]'', which also introduced the [[Witches of Dathomir]] and a [[Battle of Dathomir (Hunt for Zsinj)|battle]] against the Imperial [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Zsinj]].''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' The author wished to write a romance with humor and heart, as well as to develop settings where women were in power for fans and future creators{{WebCite|url=https://starwarsinterviews.com/various/authors/dave-wolverton-author|text=Dave Wolverton (Author)|author=Pellegrom, Dennis|work=[https://starwarsinterviews.com Star Wars Interviews]|archivedate=20200619073321|nolive=1}} to draw Force users from. Keeping in mind the adage "power corrupts," Farland wanted to explore Force users who were neither Jedi nor Sith. He intended to show a society that was "perhaps more 'tribal' in its orientation" and used power without necessarily becoming corrupted, with some Nightsister witches being "more concerned with building a world that they could live in." Farland was also in contact with fellow authors [[Kevin J. Anderson]] and [[Rebecca Moesta]], and Dathomir was first officially mentioned in ''[[Star Wars]]'' Anderson's novel ''[[Jedi Search]]'', which was published as the first installment of the [[Star Wars: The Jedi Academy Trilogy|''The Jedi Academy Trilogy'']] by Bantam Spectra in March 1994. ===''The Clone Wars''=== ====Developing Asajj Ventress==== Dathomir was brought to the silver screen by ''The Clone Wars'', based on an idea from ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator [[George Lucas]] to develop the character of Asajj Ventress, who had appeared in several episodes of the series. The series' writers discussed exploring stories from the perspectives of "villains" and also what Ventress' existence as a Sith acolyte may mean in relation to the Sith Rule of Two. Lucas really liked her character, having re-used her design drawn by [[Dermot Power]] for the Sith villain in his [[2002]] [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] who, in a change of plan, would become Count Dooku when Sir [[Christopher Lee]] joined the cast.{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/nightsisters-trivia-gallery|text="Nightsisters" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 1}} Dathomir entered ''The Clone Wars'' series when the writers came across the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Jedi Alliance]]'',{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/nightsisters-trivia-gallery|text="Nightsisters" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 4}} which was released in [[2008]] by [[LucasArts]] and featured Nightsisters led by [[Yansu Grjak]] and [[Sai Sircu]] who allied with [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] and [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Ventress]].''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Jedi Alliance]]'' This followed the larger ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'' game in [[2006]], with its [[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption|''Forces of Corruption'']] expansion featuring Dathomir's witch [[Silri]] and her search for a [[Carbonite Sith Army|hibernating army]],''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]'' but ''Jedi Alliance'' re-used concept art of witch-like characters that was originally made for the [[1999]] prequel trilogy film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. Seeing this, Lucas decided that Ventress was also a Nightsister from Dathomir. The writers of ''The Clone Wars'' then spent time consulting stories from the Expanded Universe, such as the 1990s novels and [[Pat Mills]]' [[Star Wars: Infinity's End|''Infinity's End'']] comic issues published between [[2000]] and [[2001]] for the [[Star Wars: Republic|''Republic'']] series—which pictured Dathomir's society before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and their relation to an [[Kwa/Legends|ancient civilization]]—to develop Ventress' background as a witch from Dathomir for a trilogy of animated episodes. Among the resources the writers used is [[Wookieepedia]], the unofficial online ''Star Wars'' encyclopedia.{{HomeVideoCite|set=Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Three|featurette=Witches and Monsters}} [[Katie Lucas]] took on the task of writing the trilogy, with supervising director [[Dave Filoni]] encouraging her to incorporate past story material about Ventress that would have been "near and dear" to many fans. She was also inspired by the 1915 American novel [[Wikipedia:Herland (novel)|''Herland'']] by [[Wikipedia:Charlotte Perkins Gilman|Charlotte Perkins Gilman]] in writing Dathomir's matriarchal society. Katie Lucas enjoyed the writers' room sessions where they hashed out the Dathomir episodes, which were then directed by [[Giancarlo Volpe]] and [[Kyle Dunlevy]]. The episodes presented the crew of ''The Clone Wars'' their first opportunity to develop an environment that would be revisited multiple times. With computer graphics lighting effects supervised by [[Joel Aron]] of [[Lucasfilm Animation]], creating Dathomir allowed the animators to fine-tune their lighting and shadow techniques for both characters and large assets in their surroundings, including trees, roots, and burial pods. ====Expanding Dathomir==== George Lucas had another idea for ''The Clone Wars''—to bring back Maul, the villain of ''The Phantom Menace''. The writers initially thought that doing so would be narratively difficult despite Maul's popularity with fans, and they settled on creating Maul's kin, the Nightbrothers, placing them on Dathomir as a part of the Nightsisters' society. Dathomir would serve as the setting where Ventress would do to Maul's brother, Savage Opress, what Dooku had done to her as part of Ventress' Dathomir trilogy in season three.{{SW|url=video/monster-episode-featurette|text="Monster" Episode Featurette}} Producer [[Cary Silver]] was keen on the Dathomir's Nightbrothers being their own dynamic characters despite using Maul's iconic design, and [[Kilian Plunkett]]'s art department made a conscious effort not to equate them with Maul's Sith aesthetics in their clothing and village. Later episodes of ''The Clone Wars'' featuring Dathomir were also written by Katie Lucas and broadcast as part of [[The Clone Wars: Season Four|season four]] in [[2012]]. "[[Massacre]]" centred on the Battle of Dathomir, followed by "[[Bounty (episode)|Bounty]]" following Ventress off-world, while Maul returned to Dathomir in the episodes "[[Brothers (episode)|Brothers]]" and "[[Revenge (episode)|Revenge]]." The writer listened to the 1994 album [[Wikipedia:Live Through This|''Live Through This'']] by the band [[Wikipedia:Hole (band)|Hole]] while writing the episodes, and she had also read the tragedy of Ventress in the ''Republic'' comic series and wanted to set Ventress on an independent path beholden to no one, hence leaving Dathomir to become a bounty hunter.''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Darth
